pages.title: Liquid Software
pages.description: Information provides continuity. Human decisions define the boundaries. Intelligence fulfills needs, with software adapting to actual usage.

pages.title: Core concepts
pages.description: Fifteen independently useful concepts connect information continuity, adaptive experiences, capability economics, purposeful learning, parallel evolution and outcome verification.

pages.title: Liquid Software
pages.description: Implementations emerge, adapt, stabilize and retire around actual needs, within durable semantics and human-defined boundaries.
pages.definition: Implementations emerge, adapt, stabilize and retire around actual needs, within durable semantics and human-defined boundaries.
pages.thesis: Separate useful capabilities from the lifetime of any particular implementation.
principles: Compare cumulative net value and retained flexibility
pages.scope: The emergence, stabilization, adaptation and retirement of implementations; not a requirement to regenerate every program.

related_external_work.title: A Vision of Liquid Software; associated book Liquid Software: How to Achieve Trusted Continuous Updates in the DevOps World
Malleable Software: Restoring User Agency in a World of Locked-Down Apps

pages.title: The Adaptive Interface
pages.description: Presentation and interaction respond to what is needed, by whom, where and why; how is a contextual result.
pages.definition: Presentation and interaction respond to what is needed, by whom, where and why; how is a contextual result.
pages.thesis: Derive the form of interaction from the task and participant while preserving recognizable meaning and control.
principles: Keep authority distinct from visual availability
pages.scope: Human and agent interaction, presentation and accessibility; does not imply permission to change data or policy.

related_external_work.title: Malleable Software: Restoring User Agency in a World of Locked-Down Apps

pages.title: Capture for Unknown Future Value
pages.description: Preserve appropriate source richness before anticipated questions determine the full extent of what remains.
pages.definition: Preserve appropriate source richness before anticipated questions determine the full extent of what remains.
pages.thesis: Future questions can benefit from appropriate source richness that present task models would discard.
principles: Balance future usefulness with retention purpose
Separate source preservation from processing investment
pages.scope: Purpose-bound capture and preservation; not indiscriminate collection or permanent retention of everything.

related_external_work.title: Local-first software: You own your data, in spite of the cloud
MyLifeBits — project overview and publication list

pages.title: Adaptive Information Retrieval
pages.description: Interpret emerging questions and evolve retrieval structures around observed needs while preserving source evidence and agreed meaning.
pages.definition: Interpret emerging questions and evolve retrieval structures around observed needs while preserving source evidence and agreed meaning.
pages.thesis: Retrieval structures can change with emerging questions without turning their answers into authoritative source information.
principles: Treat indexes and interpretations as revisable
Separate source preservation from processing investment
pages.scope: Question interpretation, retrieval and derived structures; not guaranteed truth or unrestricted access.

related_external_work.title: A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks

pages.title: Intelligence First, Software Second
pages.description: Establish the ability to understand and fulfill a need before choosing where dedicated software provides a useful optimization.
pages.definition: Establish the ability to understand and fulfill a need before choosing where dedicated software provides a useful optimization.
pages.thesis: Establish a bounded ability to fulfill a need before deciding which repeated paths deserve dedicated software.
principles: Start from needs and shared semantics
Materialize software when evidence supports it
Include time to value and full lifecycle costs
pages.scope: Capability fulfillment and implementation selection; intelligence still requires an operating substrate.

related_external_work.title: No Silver Bullet: Essence and Accidents of Software Engineering

pages.title: Degrees of Decision Freedom
pages.description: Higher-level decisions define the contextual space in which humans and delegated actors can make further choices.
pages.definition: Higher-level decisions define the contextual space in which humans and delegated actors can make further choices.
pages.thesis: Higher-level decisions define the space within which subsequent choices may remain open to humans or delegated actors.
principles: Keep delegated choices within applicable decisions
Make material decisions explainable and revisable
pages.scope: Contextual decision authority and delegation; not a universal scalar metric of personal freedom.

pages.title: The Self-Optimizing Information System
pages.description: Observe actual fulfillment and propose useful changes to implementations and retrieval structures under explicit authority.
pages.definition: Observe actual fulfillment and propose useful changes to implementations and retrieval structures under explicit authority.
pages.thesis: Optimize risk-adjusted cumulative net value across feasible realizations while preserving accepted meaning and authority.
principles: Require authority for material policy changes
pages.scope: Evidence-driven adaptation of retrieval and implementation; not an unrestricted autonomous policy maker.

related_external_work.title: No Silver Bullet: Essence and Accidents of Software Engineering
Malleable software in the age of LLMs

pages.title: Documentation as Executable Foundations
pages.description: Shared terminology, capability requirements and guidance preserve meaning while implementations and operational choices evolve.
pages.definition: Shared terminology, capability requirements and guidance preserve meaning while implementations and operational choices evolve.
pages.thesis: Shared documentation can preserve stable meaning while interfaces, contracts and implementations are generated for a particular need.
principles: Keep descriptive meaning distinct from authorization
Treat generated artifacts as derived realizations
pages.scope: Documentation as an interpretable foundation; not an assertion that prose alone executes or proves conformance.

related_external_work.title: Capability Documentation / Capability Requirements Document framework

pages.title: Capability Economics
pages.description: Compare feasible realizations by risk-adjusted cumulative net value over time, including full lifecycle costs and retained flexibility.
pages.definition: Compare feasible ways of fulfilling a capability by the risk-adjusted cumulative net value they deliver over time, including their full lifecycle and the flexibility they retain or remove.
pages.thesis: Choose realizations and their timing through informed comparison of full value rather than runtime price or a presumed maturity progression.
principles: Define accepted outcomes and feasibility first
Compare cumulative value and full lifecycle costs
pages.scope: A conceptual selection and evaluation framework, not a universal failure-rate claim, vendor benchmark, or mandate to replace software.

pages.description: Compose enduring information and authority with adaptive interaction, fulfillment and governed optimization.

pages.title: Liquid Software: a general introduction
pages.description: Understand the foundations, how the ideas fit together and what remains to be tested.

reader.label: General understanding
reader.perspective: a reader seeking a general introduction
reader.question: What should remain dependable when software can change more easily?
focus: Information continuity, shared meaning, authority and adaptable implementations.
Independent concepts, including learning at a different rate from operational change.
Stable experiences, parallel choices and one bounded everyday example.

reading.why: Begin with the supplied overall argument.
Understand the paradigm and reversible lifecycle.
Read the executive synthesis and stable-experience discussion.
See which concerns persist and which adapt.

pages.title: Liquid Software for business leaders
pages.description: Examine earlier accepted value, durable organizational knowledge, delegation and the ability to change direction.

reader.label: Business leaders
reader.perspective: a business leader or team owner
reader.question: How can we deliver value sooner while retaining the ability to change direction?
focus: Capability ownership, earlier value and retained organizational knowledge.
Review purpose and depth, market triggers and learning about the review process.
Internal throughput, external fitness, stable operations and verified customer outcomes.

reading.why: Frame feasible strategies and their full value.
Define delegated and reserved decisions.
Choose useful review purposes, depth and timing.
Read change choices and the customer-verification loop.

pages.title: Liquid Software for finance and investment
pages.description: Compare feasible strategies using future demand, timing, full lifecycle costs, uncertainty and reversibility.

reader.label: Finance and investment
reader.perspective: a finance leader, procurement analyst or investor assessing capability implementation
reader.question: Which feasible strategy delivers the best cumulative net value over the relevant horizon?
focus: Future demand, timing, incremental costs, uncertainty and full lifecycle value.
Stability, disruption, parallel upkeep and separate release/adoption decisions.
Explicit assumptions, avoiding double-counting, and evidence that changes an investment choice.

reading.why: Begin with the horizon-based comparison.
Use the optional structure for an inspectable assessment.
Read the worked costs and value scenarios.
Account for the path to improvement and continuing support.
Read chapter 4 and the measurement limits.

pages.title: Liquid Software for product and engineering
pages.description: Understand stable meaning, evolving contracts, contextual interfaces and selective agent, software and hybrid realizations.

reader.label: Product and engineering
reader.perspective: a product designer, architect or developer
reader.question: What must remain stable so implementation can change without changing the promise?
focus: Capability meaning, accepted outcomes and realization-specific contracts.
Languages, formats and dynamically prepared schemas under applicable protocol guarantees.
Validated reasoning compilation, invalidation, compatible parallel versions and stable contextual experiences.

reading.why: Start with purpose, terminology and meaningful scope.
Examine languages, schemas and agreements.
Read validation, assumptions and revalidation of exact portions.
Separate candidate testing, release, adoption and retirement.
Read chapters 5–7 and scenario B with the diagrams.

pages.title: Liquid Software for data and knowledge
pages.description: Separate appropriate source preservation from processing investment, then assess discovery, freshness and retrieval demand.

reader.label: Data and knowledge
reader.perspective: a data steward, knowledge worker or person managing their own information
reader.question: What should we preserve, and which processing should we invest in as needs emerge?
focus: Appropriate originals, accepted assertions, inferred assessments and derived structures.
Persisted understanding with provenance, confidence, dependencies and invalidation.
Purpose, rights, freshness and selective preparation compared with repeated reconstruction.

reading.why: Separate appropriate source preservation from predicted questions.
Compare retrieval strategies and retained understanding.
See how different reviews reuse evidence and assessments.
Read sections 2.2 and 7.3 and their vendor-evidence limits.

pages.title: Liquid Software for governance and policy
pages.description: Examine represented principals, delegated freedom, accountability and obligations that must survive adaptation.

reader.label: Governance and policy
reader.perspective: a governance, policy or risk reader
reader.question: How can adaptation preserve accountability and meaningful control?
focus: Requester, principal, beneficiary and actual information authority.
Review, decision, release, adoption and retirement as separate consequences.
User control, enforceable obligations and personal/organizational context boundaries.

reading.why: Understand delegation and retained human decisions.
Identify principal, evidence and governance boundaries.
Examine compatibility, adoption and retirement obligations.
Read sections 4.3, 6.3, 9.2 and scenario D.

pages.title: Liquid Software for research and education
pages.description: Separate conceptual proposals, source lineage and illustrative examples, and frame comparisons that can test the claims.

reader.label: Research and education
reader.question: Which learning, stability and outcome claims can be tested, and how do their sources differ?
focus: Same-origin supplied sources versus independently established prior work.
Matched feasible baselines, cohort differences, learning quality, transition costs and negative results.
Testable stability and outcome claims with vendor and illustrative evidence kept distinct.

reading.why: Read the overall claim before testing its parts.
Trace the independent originals and read-scope limits.
Read chapter 11 and the source evidence note.
Examine how review policy can be evaluated.
Distinguish conceptual maturity, worked assumptions and research questions.

pages.title: Layered Intelligence Cycles
pages.description: Reviews need distinct purposes and depths as well as suitable cadence and triggers.
pages.definition: Organize reviews around distinct purposes and depths, using suitable recurring cadences and evidence-triggered exceptions while preserving their decision boundaries.
pages.thesis: Review purpose, depth and authority precede the choice of calendar.
principles: Use event triggers alongside recurring reviews
pages.scope: Review organization and reusable understanding; not a universal schedule or mandatory hierarchy.
pages.citation: Loikkanen, Valto (conceptual source). Layered Intelligence Cycles. AI-assisted concept research paper, version 0.1.0, 28 November 2026.

pages.title: Meta-Learning: Review the Learning Process
pages.description: Evaluate how the system notices, reviews and learns, including false triggers, missed signals and unnecessary change.
pages.definition: Evaluate and improve the system's reviews, evidence use and change triggers under explicit authority, using outcomes and errors to assess how it learns.
pages.thesis: Evaluate the learning process separately from the operations it examines.
principles: Review missed signals and false triggers
pages.scope: Organizational review and learning policy; not a survey of all technical meta-learning methods.
pages.citation: Loikkanen, Valto (conceptual source). Meta-Learning: Review the Learning Process. AI-assisted concept research paper, version 0.1.0, 28 November 2026.

pages.title: Stability-Aware Evolution
pages.description: Compare improvements with transition effects, giving stable operation and familiar experience explicit value.
pages.definition: Compare feasible improvements together with transition effects, disruption, risk and continuing support costs, giving dependable operation and familiar experience explicit value.
pages.thesis: A valuable destination can be reached through a harmful transition.
principles: Compare paths as well as endpoints
Account for transition and support once
pages.scope: Feasible evolution and transition accounting; not a universal numeric valuation or unconditional refusal of change.
pages.citation: Loikkanen, Valto (conceptual source). Stability-Aware Evolution. AI-assisted concept research paper, version 0.1.0, 28 November 2026.

pages.title: Parallel Realizations
pages.description: Release, adoption and retirement can be separate decisions for compatible realizations of a capability.
pages.definition: Maintain and evaluate compatible realizations of a capability separately from decisions about their release, adoption and retirement.
pages.thesis: A new version need not replace every existing realization.
principles: Account for support and deliberate retirement
pages.scope: Compatible candidate and active realizations; not indefinite support for every version or guaranteed optional security changes.
pages.citation: Loikkanen, Valto (conceptual source). Parallel Realizations. AI-assisted concept research paper, version 0.1.0, 28 November 2026.

pages.title: Reasoning Compilation
pages.description: Materialize formally checkable portions with validation, assumptions, provenance and invalidation conditions.
pages.definition: Convert formally checkable portions of repeated reasoning into validated executable structures while retaining assumptions, provenance, limits and conditions for revalidation.
pages.thesis: Repeated formalizable reasoning can become reusable executable structure without freezing arbitrary judgment.
pages.scope: Proposed compilation capability and its validation; not an installed Skill or a guarantee that determinism establishes truth.
pages.citation: Loikkanen, Valto (conceptual source). Reasoning Compilation. AI-assisted concept research paper, version 0.1.0, 28 November 2026.

pages.title: Outcome Verification
pages.description: Connect signals, decisions and execution to whether the beneficiary’s original need improved.
pages.definition: Examine whether the beneficiary's original need improved after action, preserving the connection between signals, decisions, execution and lived results.
pages.thesis: Completed work is partial evidence; verify the original need.
principles: Retain the original problem and context
Assess internal throughput and external fitness
pages.scope: Beneficiary outcome evidence and customer-side feedback; not unrestricted collection or independently verified vendor performance.
pages.citation: Loikkanen, Valto (conceptual source). Outcome Verification. AI-assisted concept research paper, version 0.1.0, 28 November 2026.
